question: A 78-year-old man presents with fatigue and exertional dyspnea. The patient says that symptoms onset gradually 4 weeks ago and have not improved. He denies any history of anemia or nutritional deficiency. Past medical history is significant for ST-elevation myocardial infarction 6 months ago, status post coronary artery bypass graft, complicated by recurrent hemodynamically unstable ventricular tachycardia. Current medications are rosuvastatin, aspirin, and amiodarone. His blood pressure is 100/70 mm Hg, the pulse is 71/min, the temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), and the respiratory rate is 16/min. On physical examination, patient appears lethargic and tired. Skin is dry and coarse, and there is generalized pitting edema present. A complete blood count (CBC) and a peripheral blood smear show evidence of normochromic, normocytic anemia. Additional laboratory tests reveal decreased serum level of iron, decreased TIBC (total iron-binding capacity) and increased serum level of ferritin. Which of the following is the most likely etiology of the anemia in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Normochromic, normocytic anemia" -> "Decreased serum iron level" -> "Decreased TIBC" -> "Increased serum ferritin level" -> "Anemia of chronic disease" -> 95% CHAIN: "Normochromic, normocytic anemia" -> "Decreased serum iron level" -> "Decreased TIBC" -> "Increased serum ferritin level" -> "Chronic inflammation" -> "Anemia of chronic disease" -> 90% CHAIN: "Normochromic, normocytic anemia" -> "Decreased serum iron level" -> "Decreased TIBC" -> "Increased serum ferritin level" -> "Underlying chronic illness" -> "Anemia of chronic disease" -> 95%
enhanced_information: The most likely etiology of the anemia in this patient is anemia of chronic disease, supported by the findings of normochromic, normocytic anemia, decreased serum iron level, decreased TIBC, and increased serum ferritin level. The evidence paths of serum ferritin measurement, chronic disease, and chronic inflammation align with this consensus-based conclusion.
analysis: The patient's presentation with normochromic, normocytic anemia, along with decreased serum iron, decreased TIBC, and increased serum ferritin levels, is highly suggestive of anemia of chronic disease. This type of anemia commonly occurs in the setting of chronic inflammation or infection, as seen in conditions like heart failure, chronic infections, or malignancies. Given the patient's history of recurrent ventricular tachycardia post-coronary artery bypass graft and the laboratory findings, anemia of chronic disease is the most likely etiology.
